newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-M.Clark aims to stabilise cider sales.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-M.Clark aims to stabilise cider sales.

text.p: British cider maker Matthew Clark Plc, whose market share slumped as a result of booming "alcopop" sales and an industry price war, is looking to stabilise sales before aiming again for the strong growth of the early 1990s.

"We're looking to stabilise the cider market in the short term and in the medium term to go back to the sort of growth we enjoyed over the past 10 years," business development director Peter Huntley said in a telephone interview.

The cider industry had been growing by around seven percent a year in the 1990s until the phenomenal growth in popularity of "alcopops" -- alcoholic lemonades and sodas -- contributed to sales declining some three percent in the last financial year.

Matthew Clark's share of the cider market fell to 37 percent from 41 percent in year to April, while the share of its bigger rival H.P. Bulmer Holdings Plc climbed to 54.5 percent -- its highest level for over 30 years.
"We believe the situation has stabilised a lot, in the cider industry and in Matthew Clark," said Huntley.
The company reported a four percent drop in pre-tax profit for the year to April 30 to 40.6 million pounds ($68.2 million).
"The numbers are in line with consensus forecasts which is very reassuring for a share price that's been discounting a dividend cut for a long time," said one analyst who declined to be identified.
Matthew Clark's share price slumped by some 60 percent from about 670 pence following its profits warning in September. The share stood 4.0 pence higher at 246-1/2 pence at 1245 GMT.
The company maintained a total dividend of 24 pence a share.

"The comments they've given suggest that the dividend won't be cut in the future," the analyst said, adding that if they do manage to stabilise their performance the share price could see a "big move upwards".

The company has sharply increased advertising in the new financial year to nine million pounds from two million for its key Diamond White and Blackthorn ciders, as its attempt to claw back drinkers who switched over to "alcopops". Sales of Diamond White, the Diamond range and K cider had fallen by 26 percent.
"It's still early days so we can't really comment on what we've seen coming back yet...but the way it's been received by the trade, it's going very well at the moment," Huntley said.
It was not only soaring alcopop sales, but the disruption integrating its Taunton Cider business and the severe price war which caused Matthew Clark to lose market share to Bulmers.
But Huntley said the price war has subsided and that "sanity returned this year".
As for current trading, "All the markets in which we compete -- cider, wines and wholesaling -- are all very competitive and our trading at the moment is flat," Huntley said.

"They are confident the decline in trading has stabilised. They haven't quoted any volume performance since the year-end, but we think we'll see only a modest fall in profits this year and that they look exceptionally lower rated at the moment and look good value for money," the analyst said.
He expected pre-tax profits of around 38 million pounds in the new financial year.
